pattern.crimePattern: a foundation's programmes officer strangles the finance director who has found nine years of grants to a shell company's till, then has the server backups wiped
pattern.notes: Fictional foundation, staff and family; Runda is a setting only. Maina Kabiru is the "M." of cases 95, 97 and 98. The Chair, Margaret Kabiru, is in Mombasa and is not the killer here. Advocate Wanjiru Nderitu is conflicted as a Msingi Trust director (case 91) and is replaced after the first interview.

facts.text: Zipporah Naliaka was found dead in the Ukarimu Foundation's archive room in Runda on Friday morning.
Strangled with a narrow cord. Her key-fob lanyard is gone from her neck.
Approvals: nine years of monthly "community grants" to Till 880 214, plus Kadzo's "history", the spa sponsorship and Mlinzi Bora, all by M. Kabiru "per Chair", signed.
Her audit laptop is missing; its charger is still plugged in at the archive table.
Fob log, Thursday: Zipporah into the archive at 20:40; Maina into the archive at 20:52 and out at 21:15.
Fob log: Philip used only the main-house doors on Thursday evening, and left at 21:30.
Server logs: at 07:58 on Friday "mkabiru" opened a ticket, "Backups full, please clear"; at 08:12 "tmburu" deleted them all. The server keeps 90 days and was never cleared before.
Jemimah: "Mr. Maina was here before me on Friday, at quarter past six, in the archive with the door shut. He never comes before nine. Madam always wore her fob round her neck."
Jemimah was at home until she came in at 06:30 on Friday.
The gate guard's book: no visitor after 18:00 on Thursday; staff fobs only.
Under a magnifier, the Chair's "signature" is identical on every approval: the same ink halo, the same nick in the M. A facsimile stamp.
Philip's email: a job interview on Thursday afternoon, and a resignation draft saved at 20:10.
The choir: Geoffrey was at practice in Kahawa, 19:00–21:30, in their video.
Geoffrey: last week she said, "If I'm right about these grants, I'll have to leave and we'll need my pension."
Gala broadcast and hotel: Margaret Kabiru was in Mombasa, on stage at 21:00.
The Thika client's book: Tony was there 18:00–22:30 on Thursday.
A Gigiri receipt: Advocate Nderitu at dinner, 19:30–22:15.
Records ①: Thursday 21:20, five minutes after leaving the archive, Maina called a number saved as "Shosh" for 3 minutes.
Records ①: Maina's PesaPap paid Kadzo Mwamuye and Sagal Ahmed; an Ukarimu "petty cash" line tops up Till 880 214.
Records ②: nine years of foundation transfers to Till 880 214's settlement account, the Msingi Trust: KSh 214 million.
In Maina's flat: Zipporah's audit laptop.
In a jacket pocket in Maina's flat: Zipporah's key-fob lanyard.
Fingerprints taken from Maina in detention.
Post-mortem: strangled with a narrow flat cord about 1.5 cm wide, like a lanyard; no head injury, nothing in the blood.
Post-mortem: death on Thursday between 20:50 and 21:20.
Lab: the ligature mark matches the lanyard's weave; Zipporah's hair is caught in its clip.
Lab: Zipporah's and Maina's prints on the laptop lid.
Missing: three months of server backups were deleted the morning after.
Missing: her audit laptop is gone.
Missing: her lanyard is gone from her neck.
Missing: the Chair never signed anything by hand.
Missing: the gate guard logged no visitor.

Maina: "Every grant was approved by the Chair."
Maina: "Shosh said, 'Fix it, Maina.' I've been fixing things for her since I was nineteen. Envelopes, grants, people. I didn't know how to fix Zipporah." His advocate stops him.
Maina: "I never touched her lanyard."
Tony: "The backups failed on their own."
Tony: "Maina opened a ticket at eight saying they were full. I cleared them. I'm a contractor; I do tickets."

Kabiru: "I was in Mombasa. Maina is unwell; he has been for years. The foundation's finances are a matter for its officers."

interrogations.intro: Maina sits beside Advocate Nderitu, his sweater sleeves pulled over his hands. Once reopened: "I went home at six on Thursday. Every grant was approved by the Chair."
Tony puts his laptop bag on his knees like a shield. "The backups failed on their own."
Advocate Nderitu answers before Amani has finished asking. "The foundation has never paid any PesaPap till."
Philip keeps loosening his tie. "I wasn't at the office on Thursday evening."
Geoffrey holds his choir folder. "We were having a hard year. I was at choir."
Margaret Kabiru, by phone from Mombasa, gracious and precise. "I have given forty years to this country, Detective. I hope you'll remember that when you write your report."
Mama Jemimah folds her arms and tells it plainly.

reconstruction.text: At year-end Zipporah audits the programme grants herself: nine years of monthly "community grants" to Till 880 214, approved by Maina "per Chair" with a facsimile stamp. On Wednesday she tells him she'll report it on Friday.
On Thursday at 20:40 she pulls the original files in the archive. At 20:52 Maina comes in with his fob "to explain". She won't listen. He strangles her with her own lanyard.
He takes her laptop and the lanyard and leaves at 21:15. At 21:20 he calls "Shosh".
At 06:15 on Friday he is back in the archive before anyone. At 07:58 he opens a ticket: "Backups full, please clear." At 08:12 Tony clears them.

afterVerdict.beat: Maina is charged with Zipporah's murder. His statement names his grandmother only as "Shosh said fix it." Halima: "A grandson's word against a woman with forty years of portraits on her walls. It isn't enough for Joseph. Not yet."

files.text: The paymaster: nine years of Ukarimu Foundation "community grants" to Till 880 214, KSh 214 million, through the Msingi Trust.
"Shosh said, 'Fix it, Maina.'" Margaret Kabiru's grandson; the "M." of cases 95, 97 and 98.

afterVerdict.beat: At 23:40 the airline Halima flagged after case 98 reports a booking: Margaret Kabiru, Nairobi to London, 09:15 tomorrow, booked an hour after Maina's arrest.
Mwalimu calls. She doesn't say hello. "Office 4.12. Go and get her before nine. And Amani: take your father's file with you."

clockPlan.note: Three stamps (the maximum): Maina's line, the foundation's bank, and a warrant on his flat. Maina is reopened by the fob log. Detain him after the search; prints (6 h) and fibres (12 h) inside 24 h.
